A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the mass transfer of solutes through ion exchange membranes is influenced by the hydration state of membrane counterions, which depends on the membrane soaking and on the ionic composition of the solution.
the presence of electrolytes in the solution has a limited impact on the mass transfer, but this impact is much more important if the membrane has been soaked with this electrolyte.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the electrolyte influence on the mass transfer of solute through an ion exchange material is not a simple function of the solute or solvent radius, but it is mainly governed by the hydration number of membrane counterion, which is fixed during the membrane preparation.

the presence of electrolytes in the solution can be used to tune the mass transfer through the membrane, and that the hydration state of the membrane counterions is a key parameter in the control of mass transfer.
